correctness.rationale: Every mixed-shore independent color class is exactly one deleted matched pair; every other class is pure shore. For q>=3 pairs have fewer than q vertices and cannot qualify, and >=3 pure classes divide one shore into >=2 colors none of whose vertices sees the other own-shore color. For q=2 any paired class requiring two color-dominating vertices forces every other color to be mixed (one color on each shore), hence the graph must admit full paired partition, i.e. m=n=t, excluded. Thus k>=3 impossible. The unique bipartition two-coloring of this connected non-crown graph makes all vertices color-dominating; it realizes iff q<=m. Boundary m=2,t=2,n=2 excluded; n>m or t<m ensure connectivity. Universal proof not inferred from finite checker.

This is a natural complementary classification, with close methodological overlap acknowledged rather than claiming a novel coloring technique.
